Hi Emma —

Thanks again for a productive renewal discussion last week. Per our call I attached a refreshed term sheet (Spectral_Renewal_Termsheet_v3.pdf) that reflects a 12-month renewal with a graduated commit ladder, plus a short-term bridge credit to cover the expected Q1 consumption bump. High-level summary:

- 12-mo term; tiered commit (Base / +25% / +50%) with stepped discounts at each tier
- 90-day bridge credit of $60k to smooth the migration period; applies only to overage invoice credits
- Usage collar (floor 60% of committed tokens/month) to protect both parties from extreme underutilization
- Quarterly milestone (onboarding + latency SLA validation) that will trigger a 10% additional credit if met

Can you confirm procurement's comfort level with a short escrow (bridge credit) and the collar construct? If it helps, Ben and Lauren are on copy — Lauren can outline billing mechanics and put the escrow language in the SOW.

Attached: Spectral_Renewal_Termsheet_v3.pdf; I also included a usage export for Q3 for reference.

Next step: if procurement is good with this shape, I can send a controlled DocuSign for signature and a short amendment for the SOW.

Thanks —

1) Bridge credit is attractive, but procurement prefers the credit to be held in escrow (third-party) or as an invoice credit schedule tied to milestone acceptance — they dislike unconditional up-front credits.

Hi Emma / team —

Quick note on how we can operationalize the bridge credit and collar:

- Escrow: we can either hold the bridge credit in a third-party escrow (preferred by some customers) or book it as a contra-invoice credit line that amortizes against overage invoices over the 90-day period. Both approaches are supported; escrow requires a short addendum describing the release conditions.
- Collar: instead of a fixed 60%, we can index the floor to 70% of the trailing-3-month average usage to give you alignment as usage grows. I modeled scenarios in the attached (small table in the term sheet).
- Pricing hold: we can guarantee committed-tier pricing for 6 months from the effective date. Any platform-wide price changes after that would only apply to new overage pricing; committed-tier rates are locked for the hold period.

If you give the go-ahead on the escrow approach, I will prepare the SOW language and a short escrow addendum for legal review. Ben — tagging you to confirm concession bandwidth if we front $60k as bridge credit in escrow.
